reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossover identification device for container substitution: holding the optimized instruction and the test instances fixed, compare the gain of the memory bank distilled from the same training episodes that instruction was optimized on (cells 6, 10) against the gain of a bank distilled from a disjoint half (cells 7, 9), so that the resulting Delta_info is attributable to shared episode provenance rather than to headroom, level, or token budget.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three, in descending threat. (1) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) already puts ReasoningBank, Memento and GEPA on identical 528/267 trajectories with Qwen3.5-27B as a backbone; the proposal honestly concedes this and withdraws its v2 novelty sentence. What survives is the combined cell and the crossover, which EvoAgentBench genuinely lacks — but this narrows the contribution from 'first three-way comparison' to 'a provenance contrast added to an existing table.' (2) MIPROv2 (2406.11695) is the framing precedent a reviewer names first: instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint on one training set is the two-container ablation, and its recurring finding that the split is task-dependent already predicts the proposal's likely 'mixed/complementarity' outcome. The retrieval read and the held-out-episode crossover are the real deltas. (3) Experience Distillation (2607.21051) measures the identical estimand shape — what fraction of an in-context gain survives when the information is moved to a second container — with weights rather than an instruction as the container. Together these leave the proposal with a real but incremental methodological delta rather than a new question.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory endpoint may be structurally powerless in the chosen environment, and a null would be uninterpretable. Delta_info requires that B_a contain content that is useful on S_test AND specific to half a. But S_train_a and S_train_b are 400-episode halves drawn by seeded stratified random split (50/30/20 by dataset) from pooled HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki, so the two halves are exchangeable by construction. The insights an ExpeL- or ReasoningBank-style distiller extracts from 400 random multi-hop QA episodes are overwhelmingly generic ('decompose the question, find the bridge entity, verify with a second search'), and B_a and B_b will therefore carry near-identical content. If so, Delta_info is near zero no matter whether substitution is real, and outcome (ii) 'complementarity' would be reported when the truth is 'the own/other contrast had no content difference to operate on.' Nothing in the design certifies otherwise: the procedural positive control B_a+proc10 certifies sensitivity to INSTANCE-specific value on 100 targeted S_test items, which is a different quantity from HALF-specific value; no preregistered statistic measures semantic divergence between B_a and B_b, and no crossover-specific positive control exists. The proposal's own numbers make this acute — with own-gain ~2pt and other-gain ~4.5pt the expected Delta_info is ~2.5pt against a stated MDE of 1.8-3.1pt and a claim threshold of 2pt, and any realistic degree of half-exchangeability pushes the true effect under the floor. Compounding this: the paper's title claim ('memory is just an un-optimized prompt') is carried by Prediction 4, a level equivalence at full data, which is only descriptive; and its TOST margins are wider than the effects being compared. 'I1_ab x C_ab within 4pt of I1_ab x M_ab' and 'I0 x C_a TOST-equivalent to I0 x M_a at +/-4pt' will pass even if compilation destroys the entire memory effect, since the field's bank effects on this model class are +0.6 to +3.6pt. As specified, the compile-once recommendation is close to unfalsifiable.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Split the two halves by task structure rather than at random — by question template / reasoning schema in E1, and by ALFWorld task type in E2 — so that B_a and B_b carry genuinely non-exchangeable procedural content and the own/other contrast has purchase. Random stratified halving actively destroys the signal the crossover is built to detect. (2) Preregister a bank-divergence measurement (item-level semantic overlap and cross-half retrieval rate: how often the top-7 items from B_a and B_b for the same test instance are paraphrases) and report it before unblinding; if the halves are exchangeable, Delta_info's null is uninformative and must be reported as such rather than as complementarity. (3) Add a positive control for the crossover contrast itself, not just for instance-specific value: seed each half with half-marked content of known usefulness and verify the crossover recovers it, exactly as proc10 does for the instance dimension. (4) Promote the level test — I1_ab x M_ab vs max(I1_ab x M0, I0 x M_ab) — to confirmatory and power it, since it, not Delta_info, is what the title asserts, and tighten the TOST margins from +/-4pt to something smaller than the memory effect being compared (e.g. +/-1.5pt), accepting that this costs n. (5) Define the iso-cost arm. (6) Reconsider G7's 4pt threshold: the proposal cites the field's own range as +0.6 to +3.6pt, so by its own literature it has preregistered a gate the modal world fails, and n=300 with SE~2.4pt makes the gate decision close to a coin flip in either direction.
reviews.missing_baseline: A compute-matched inference control: spend memory's injection budget on inference instead of on context. Memory injection at k=7 costs both tokens and prefill; a reviewer will demand that the no-memory agent be given the equivalent budget as extra tool calls (e.g. 11 rather than 8) or self-consistency at k=2-3 with majority vote, and will suspect that this alone recovers most of the +0.6 to +3.6pt bank gain. I3 does not cover this — padding I0 with task-generic boilerplate is a deliberately useless use of the budget and only bounds a length artifact, not a compute-reallocation rival. This matters most for the paper's efficiency recommendation ('the second container is cheaper to serve'), which is asserted but never measured against a cost-matched alternative. Notably, an 'iso-cost' arm appears twice in the submission — 4,400 episodes in the Tier 2 compute arithmetic, and first in the Tier 2 contingency cut order — but is defined nowhere: it has no artifact entry, no cell in the 25-row grid, no prediction, and no membership in any Holm family. Secondary omission: no truly out-of-distribution bank (items distilled from a different corpus or task) as a negative control for presence-of-retrieval effects; the shuffled-bank sanity check is mentioned only in passing in Ablations and never given a cell or an n.
reviews.preprint_collision: Well above the standard for this section, and it should be credited: a dated scan (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), 15 named HuggingFace Papers queries over 244 papers, by-id verification for 54 arXiv IDs, committed scan records, an explicit two-channel rule for dropping a citation, a correction that reinstates five papers wrongly retracted in v2, and a withdrawal of the v2 novelty sentence in light of EvoAgentBench. That is a real search, not a gesture, and I found no preprint in my own knowledge that already runs an own-bank-vs-other-bank crossover at a fixed optimized instruction. Three concrete weaknesses remain. (a) The single most novelty-threatening paper, EvoAgentBench (2607.05202), was verified from a PDF supplied by the PI while arXiv is unreachable from the compute node — so every load-bearing absence claim ('no combined optimizer-plus-memory condition', 'the word token-matching does not occur', 'no paired test') rests on a source no reviewer can independently check, and a web snippet in the same submission is already documented as having misreported that paper's numbers (+7 vs the PDF's +3.6). If any of those absences is wrong, the contribution collapses to the crossover alone. (b) The proposal itself flags that the appendix of 2608.14036 has not been opened — appendices are precisely where a GEPA-plus-memory ablation would sit, and the residual-risk paragraph names that exact scenario. Flagging a hole is not closing it. (c) Coverage of the most dangerous window is thin: arXiv unreachable, Semantic Scholar rate-limited without a key, so the last two months are effectively HuggingFace-Papers-only (44 papers dated >= 2026-06), which is a popularity-biased sample and systematically misses the untrending preprint most likely to scoop a measurement paper. Net: the check is a strength of the submission, but the novelty argument is single-sourced at its most critical point.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossover identification device for agentic-memory evaluation: holding the optimized instruction and the test instances fixed, compare the gain of the bank distilled from the very episodes that instruction was optimized on (own) against the gain of a bank from episodes the optimizer never saw (other), so that the shrinkage of memory's benefit under prompt optimization can be attributed to information the instruction absorbed rather than to headroom it consumed — with a fix/break signature to separate absorption from interference, and a compiled-bank arm token-matched against live per-instance retrieval.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, in different ways. (a) EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202) is the empirical threat: it already puts ReasoningBank (+3.6), Memento (-2.4) and GEPA (+1.2) on the same 528/267 trajectories on Qwen3.5-27B — one of this proposal's own candidate agents — so a reviewer can read 'an optimizer given the same episodes nearly matches a memory retriever' directly off a published table, which is most of the rhetorical force of the title. The proposal is right that it lacks combined optimizer+memory cells, token matching, a compiled arm and paired statistics, so the *attribution* is not pre-empted; but it caps how surprising the headline can be. (b) MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695) is the conceptual threat: instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint optimization on one training set is exactly the two-container ablation, with the published finding that the split is task-dependent. The proposal's genuine deltas over MIPROv2 are the query-conditioned read, distillation, and the held-out-episode crossover — real, but incremental. Neither runs the own-vs-other contrast, so novelty survives; it survives as a refinement of attribution on a question the field has already half-answered, not as a new question.
reviews.strongest_objection: The design is very likely to terminate in one of its own fallback branches, and every branch is a weaker paper than the title. Do the arithmetic on gate G7: the crossover (cells 5-10) only carries a confirmatory claim if the *unseen* bank M_b still adds >=4pt (lower 80% CI >=2pt) on top of an optimized instruction I1a, and then Prediction 1 additionally needs own to trail other by >=2pt. So the study needs roughly a 4-6pt memory effect surviving prompt optimization on a 27-32B agent in BM25 multi-hop QA. The proposal's own cited priors say that is implausible: this program's pilot measured +0.6pt, 90% CI [-1.2, +2.5], TOST-equivalent to zero for an ExpeL bank on Qwen3.5-27B, and EvoAgentBench's best method on that same backbone is +3.6pt at a *hand-written* prompt — i.e. below the G1 bar of 4pt before any optimizer is applied, and necessarily smaller after. The pre-registered consequence of a G7 failure is that the primary becomes 'the headroom share and the ladder' with the crossover run at 2 descriptive seeds, which means the paper's advertised contribution never gets tested at power. The second half of the objection is that the branch where G7 *passes* is not much better: the proposal concedes in Limitation 12 that BM25 multi-hop QA 'is not where procedural memory is expected to be most valuable', and the procedure for HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki is roughly one paragraph ('decompose, search the bridge entity, search the second hop') — precisely the content an instruction slot holds losslessly. A positive Delta_info there is close to tautological and environment-bound, and E2 cannot rescue it because ALFWorld's own treatment-free floor of 3.8-4.6pt at n=274 exceeds the 2pt claim threshold, so the one environment with genuinely compilable recurring procedure is definitionally incapable of supporting the claim. Heads the result is unsurprising and local, tails it is a null already reported by the program's own pilot.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Screen on the effect that the design actually needs. Make G7 — memory's gain at the *optimized* instruction — the selection criterion across agent x bank x *environment*, not a downstream gate applied after A1 was chosen by its I0 effect (G1). If no in-scope cell has a surviving memory effect large enough to admit a 2pt Delta_info, that finding is the paper and should be the pre-registered primary plan, not the fallback. 2) Move the confirmatory test to an environment with recurring multi-step subroutines (ALFWorld promoted to primary, or a tool/web agent benchmark), and power it below the claim threshold — more episodes, more decoding seeds, or a per-subgoal paired metric instead of binary task success — so E2's 3.8-4.6pt floor stops disqualifying the only setting where the phenomenon should live. Demote multi-hop QA to the replication it currently calls E2. 3) Promote cell 18c (I1a x M_a^re) to Tier 0, n=1000, 4 seeds. Prediction 5 is an equivalence claim ('within 2pt') and the wording-vs-provenance alternative (outcome ii'') is the one that most directly guts 'information-specific'; at n=500 with 1 decoding seed at I0 the TOST cannot resolve 2pt, so the arm defending the headline interpretation is underpowered relative to the arm producing it. 4) Pre-register sign consistency across both crossover directions as a condition on the claim rather than merely fitting and reporting the direction x half interaction — 'no consistency across directions is required' lets a large one-directional effect plus a bank-quality asymmetry produce a significant mean Delta_info with the mechanism unidentified. 5) Pay for all of this by cutting Tier 1 hard and by collapsing the Short Hypothesis, which currently bundles five distinct claims (Delta_info, full-data non-addition, compile-once equivalence, no I2 synergy, instance-specific residual) where the track brief asks for one sharp claim.
reviews.missing_baseline: A token-matched irrelevant-content control in the memory slot — a shuffled or randomly-drawn-item bank retrieved at k=7 and injected at the same token count, run at *both* I0 and I1a. It appears only as an unnumbered 'shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check' in the last line of Baselines and Ablations, with no cell number, no n, no seed count and no compute allocation, while 25 other cells get all four. Without it, a small residual own-bank gain at I1a cannot be separated from the format effect of having anything at all in the memory slot, and the compiled-arm TOST (cell 4 vs cell 2) has no null-content anchor. Second omission: an oracle-retrieval upper bound (the best item in B_a per test instance, chosen post hoc), without which a null Delta_info or a null residual is confounded with MiniLM top-7 retrieval quality — G3 certifies only 60% relevance on a 100-item audit, far too weak to license 'memory has no non-substitutable value'. Third, smaller: there is no *informed* hand-written instruction. I_H is explicitly information-free and C_a is an LLM compiler, so the practitioner's actual alternative — a human reads the 400 episodes or the bank and writes the instruction — is never run.
reviews.preprint_collision: This is the strongest section of the submission and should be credited as such: it is dated, it lists its channels (15 HF Papers queries, 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs, targeted web search), it names the paper that broke a prior novelty claim (EvoAgentBench, arXiv 2607.05202), and it *withdraws* the v2 sentence 'no published work uses one as the control for the other' rather than defending it. It also correctly flags that the compile direction (Prediction 7) is already pre-empted in sign by arXiv 2608.14036, 2606.30775 and 2605.23899, and restates it as a quantified equivalence. I am not aware of a preprint that runs the own-vs-other held-out-episode crossover, so I do not think the core is scooped. But the check's ground truth is fragile in ways that matter for the numbers it is load-bearing for. arXiv is unreachable from the node and Semantic Scholar was rate-limited, so abs pages were confirmed 'through web search results only'; the EvoAgentBench figures that set the G1 threshold and justify the whole screening design (+3.6/+1.2/-2.4 on Qwen3.5-27B) come from a PDF 'supplied by the PI' — an interested party, not an independent channel — after a web snippet had already misreported one of those numbers as +7; and the appendix of arXiv 2608.14036 is admitted to be unopened, which is exactly where the residual risk the proposal itself names ('a GEPA + memory ablation may exist in an appendix of a systems paper') would sit. Compounding this, the section documents a prior incident in which five citations were wrongly retracted as unverifiable and then reinstated, which establishes that this pipeline errs in both directions. I could verify the pre-2026 anchors (ExpeL 2308.10144, GEPA 2507.19457, ReasoningBank 2509.25140, Memp 2508.06433, A-MEM 2502.12110, MIPROv2 2406.11695); I cannot vouch for several 2026 IDs that fall within my own knowledge, including 'Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip' (2604.14585), MemAPO (2603.21520) and TERMS-Bench (2605.13909). Verdict on the check: thorough in procedure, not yet closed in fact — the re-run before design freeze that the proposal promises should include opening 2608.14036's appendix and confirming EvoAgentBench through a channel other than the PI.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A provenance crossover that holds the optimized instruction and the test instances fixed and varies only which disjoint training half a retrieved-experience bank was distilled from (cells 6/7 and 9/10), so that the drop in memory's marginal gain can be split into an information-specific component the optimizer absorbed from the same episodes (Delta_info) and a generic headroom component that any better prompt would produce.
reviews.closest_prior_work: MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695) is the real threat, and the proposal concedes it. Its instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablations already measure how much of one training set's value each prompt container can carry, with the known finding that the split is task-dependent. A reviewer will ask whether Delta_info is more than rediscovering, with a retriever attached, that a demonstration container's marginal value falls once the instruction container has been optimized on the same data. The proposal's genuine increments over it are three: a query-conditioned read instead of static demos, distillation instead of raw exemplars, and the episode-provenance split (own vs other half) that MIPROv2 has no analogue of and that is what converts a confounded 'memory adds less' observation into an identified one. EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202, an ID I cannot independently verify) is the second threat: it reportedly places ReasoningBank, Memento and GEPA on the same 528/267 trajectories, which is the side-by-side table the earlier version of this proposal claimed did not exist. If its appendix contains any GEPA+retrieval cell, the combined-cell novelty collapses; the proposal asserts from a PI-supplied PDF that it does not. Experience Distillation (arXiv 2607.21051) already reports the same retention-ratio quantity with weights as the second container, so the ratio's shape is not new either -- only the choice of an optimized instruction as the rival container, and the crossover that makes it identifiable, are.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory endpoint is a difference between two already-small quantities, in exactly the regime the proposal's own evidence says is near zero, and the gating structure makes that worse rather than better. Delta_info is bounded above by the bank's total gain at the optimized instruction; the priors quoted in the proposal for this model class are +0.6pt (the program's own pilot, TOST-equivalent to zero for ExpeL on Qwen3.5-27B) to +3.6pt (ReasoningBank on Qwen3.5-27B). G1 then requires a >=4pt paired gain on S_dev with n=300 and SE=2.4pt, and A1 is chosen as the maximum over six agent-by-format pairings measured at that SE. That is selection on upward noise: the winner's dev estimate is inflated, its true S_test gain regresses toward the 1-3pt range, and Delta_info -- a fraction of that -- lands at roughly 1-2pt against the proposal's own stated MDE of 1.8-3.1pt. Risk factor 8 addresses only the inflation of S_raw by this selection; it does not address the deflation of power for Delta_info, which is the actual confirmatory test. The modal outcome is therefore outcome (i): a Delta_info CI covering zero, in an environment (BM25 multi-hop QA over HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki) that limitation 12 concedes is not where procedural memory is expected to be valuable. A paper reporting that memory and instruction cannot be distinguished where memory does nothing is not a finding about substitution. Compounding this: every claim a practitioner would quote is descriptive and underpowered. Prediction 4 ('I1_ab x M_ab <= max(I1_ab x M0, I0 x M_ab) + MDE', cells 12b-12d and 18b) is an accept-the-null equivalence run at 2 seeds with a ~4pt margin, and Prediction 7's compile-once claim is a TOST at +/-4pt -- a 4pt margin on a 4pt effect is not evidence of equivalence, it is a restatement of the noise floor. The paper's headline sentences would rest on its weakest arms while its best-powered arm answers a narrow mechanistic question.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Stop fixing the confirmatory environment in advance. Let the pre-registered screening choose the environment as well as the agent-by-bank pairing, or promote ALFWorld to primary -- E2 is described as the setting where task templates recur and 'procedural memory is maximally compilable', which is precisely where a substitution claim is worth making, and it is currently demoted to directional only because n=274 gives a 3.8-4.6pt floor. Buying that n (more task seeds, more decoding seeds, per-episode pairing) is a better use of compute than eighteen Tier-1 cells in an environment where the effect may not exist. (2) Gate on the contrast you actually test. G1 and G7 gate on acc(I0 x M_a) and on the unseen bank's gain, not on own-vs-other; add a dev-side estimate of the crossover contrast itself with its own floor, so the study proceeds only when the primary endpoint is measurable, not when a nuisance quantity is large. (3) Give the full-data question confirmatory status: 4 optimizer seeds on 12b-12d, and add the co-adapted full-data arm (see missing baseline), since Prediction 4 is the sentence readers will cite. (4) Cut ruthlessly. Cells 15, 18d, 20, 21, 23 and 25 are defensive; their compute belongs in seeds for cells 5-10 and 12b-12d. A 9-page paper with 25 arms, 16 predictions and five test families will be read as a program, not a result -- and if Delta_info is inconclusive, no amount of Tier-1 instrumentation rescues it.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. Primary: I2_ab -- co-adaptation at full data. Cell 11 runs I2a (optimizer with the bank in context) only on half a, so the recommended deployment (cell 12d: I1_ab x C_ab, no retrieval) and Prediction 4 are both benchmarked against an instruction that never saw the bank at the data scale being recommended. The track this was proposed for is named for coupling a self-editing memory with a prompt optimizer; an area chair will ask why the coupled system is never run at full data, and 'the bank does not add to an optimized instruction' is not established until the optimizer that was allowed to see the bank on all 800 episodes has been beaten too. Secondary: a compute- or token-matched inference-time alternative. Injected memory is token-matched only against padded prompts (I3), against the compiled block (C_a), and against raw exemplars (R_a) -- i.e. only against other things in the prompt. It is never matched against spending the same budget on more search: e.g. I0 with the step limit raised from 8 to 10-11 calls, or best-of-2 sampling with the same total tokens. On BM25 multi-hop QA that baseline plausibly beats both containers, and if it does, the entire two-container framing is answering a question whose premise (that these are the relevant places to put the budget) has not been tested.
reviews.preprint_collision: This is a substantially better check than most I see, and it should be credited: it is dated (2026-09-03, prior scan 2026-08-21), it states its channels and query counts (15 HuggingFace queries, 244 papers, 54 by-id verifications), it names the closest paper and enumerates precisely what that paper does and does not contain, and -- unusually -- it explicitly withdraws v2's sentence that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other'. That is the behavior the field should reward. But the check's own verification channel is degraded in ways that undercut the conclusion it reaches. arXiv is unreachable from the node; abstracts were confirmed through web-search snippets; and the check itself documents that one such snippet misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 when the PDF says +3.6, and that v2 retracted five citations as unverifiable that all in fact exist. So the instrument has a demonstrated error rate in both directions, and the load-bearing novelty claim -- that EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) has no combined optimizer-plus-memory condition, no token matching and no paired statistics -- rests on a single PDF supplied by the PI and checked by the authors, with no independent channel. If a GEPA-plus-retrieval cell exists in any appendix of that paper or of a 2026 systems paper, the combined-cell contribution is gone, and the check acknowledges this as residual risk without closing it (the appendix of 2608.14036 is flagged as un-opened). One adjacent literature also appears unsearched: the check hunts for 'memory vs prompt optimization' collisions but not for the design primitive it actually turns on -- held-out-episode / data-provenance crossovers in the prompt-optimization and contamination literature, i.e. work asking whether an optimizer's gain is specific to the episodes it saw. That is where a scoop of the *method* (as opposed to the application) would live. Finally, a caveat about my own judgment here: every ID cited from 2602 through 2608 postdates what I can independently verify, so I can neither confirm nor refute EvoAgentBench, MemDelta, MemHarness, Experience Distillation or the skills papers. The novelty claim consequently rests entirely on the authors' scan, which makes the degraded verification channel a real weakness rather than a formality.
